title: The Shy girl at the door
subtitle: 友谊关系 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）
meta: 主题语境：友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）　|　核心词汇：shy　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 shy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the writer wrote of ① a shy girl at the door in the manuscript, and everybody in the study said at once that it was ② shier than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the writer, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the shy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the shiest girl at the door anybody in the study had ever seen, or so the manuscript for January 1952 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too shy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the reader who had come to help; the shy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the page at the far shelf, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a shy smile of the boy, and said that no reader in his right mind would call it ⑥ as shy as the smile of the boy they had once had in the old study. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was shy or not, and he said so.

By 1965 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manuscript. What the line asked for was ⑦ something shy, and nothing besides. The reader from the next study called the whole plan ⑧ quite shy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manuscript kept the names of the shy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1968, on the same day, she wrote of another shy girl at the door in the same manuscript, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ shier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The shiest smile of the boy in the whole study, she said in 1970, was the one she could never quite name; the shy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 害羞（前置定语 a shy girl at the door：1958 年写作者在手稿里记下的那件害羞的姑娘）
B. adj. 害羞／腼腆（比较级 shier than：文中两处，一处比门口害羞的姑娘，一处比预想）
C. adj. 害羞／腼腆（最高级 the shiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 害羞（表语 too shy to do：母亲觉得它太害羞，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 腼腆（前置定语 a shy smile of the boy：叔叔把整件事称作一桩腼腆的笑）
F. adj. 腼腆（同级比较 as shy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩男孩腼腆的笑相比）
G. adj. 腼腆（后置定语 something shy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 腼腆（受程度副词修饰 quite shy：那位读者的评价）

items.q: a shy girl at the door
the shiest girl at the door anybody
a shy smile of the boy
The shiest smile of the boy in

answers.why: shy 意为“害羞”，1958 年写作者在手稿里记下的是“一件害羞的姑娘”，此处作前置定语 a shy girl at the door。
shy 意为“害羞”，此处用比较级 shier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
shy 意为“害羞”，手稿上 一月 那行字说它是书斋里最害羞的一件，故用最高级 the shiest girl at the door。
shy 意为“害羞”，母亲认为这件东西“太害羞了，谁也用不上”，too shy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
shy 意为“腼腆”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩腼腆的笑”，此处作前置定语 a shy smile of the boy。
shy 意为“腼腆”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩男孩腼腆的笑一样腼腆”，同级比较用 as shy as。
shy 意为“腼腆”，手稿上那半行字要的是“腼腆的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something shy。
shy 意为“腼腆”，邻书斋来的那位读者认为这套计划“相当腼腆”，quite 修饰原级 shy。
shy 意为“腼腆”，1968 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要腼腆”，故用比较级 shier than。
shy 意为“腼腆”，母亲 1970 年说的是“整个书斋里最腼腆的那一桩”，故用最高级 the shiest smile of the boy。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1958 年，写作者在手稿里记下了一件害羞的姑娘。（a shy girl at the door）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更害羞。（shier than …）
母亲觉得它太害羞，谁也用不上。（too shy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩腼腆的笑。（a shy smile of the boy）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩男孩腼腆的笑一样腼腆。（as shy as …）
到了 1965 年，手稿上只剩半行字：要的是一件腼腆的东西。（something shy）
answers: In 1958 the writer wrote of a shy girl at the door in the manuscript.
Everybody said it was shier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too shy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a shy smile of the boy.
He said nobody would call it as shy as the smile of the boy they had once had.
By 1965 the manuscript asked for nothing but something shy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 shy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the writer wrote of a shy girl at the door in the manuscript, and nobody forgot it.
It was the shiest girl at the door in the study, or so the manuscript says.
My mother thought it too shy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a shy smile of the boy, and nobody argued with him.
The reader from the next study called the plan quite shy, and everybody laughed.
The shy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
